skills.grammarMd:
In Kurmancî the owner comes **after** the thing, joined by a small ending, the **ezafe**:

- masculine words take **-ê**: *bavê min* my father · *birayê te* your brother · *simbêlê Hamo* Hamo’s moustache
- feminine words take **-a**: *xwişka min* my sister · *malbata me* our family · *jina wî* his wife

**dê** (mother) is irregular: *diya min* my mother, and you call her *Dayê!*

The pronouns after the ezafe are the “object” ones: **min, te, wî** (his), **wê** (her), **me, we, wan**.

Every noun is masculine or feminine, and the ending tells you which: learn *sêva min* and *nanê min* together with the words.

skills.grammarMd:
For **plural** owners and things the ezafe is **-ên**: *birayên min* my brothers · *zarokên me* our children.

After a **vowel**, a **y** slips in: *birayê min* my brother · *xwarziya min* my niece · *wêneyên me* our photos.

The ezafe can also stand alone, meaning “the one of”:

- *Ev pêlav ya min e.* This shoe is mine. (**ya** for a feminine thing)
- *Ev kum yê te ye.* This cap is yours. (**yê** for a masculine thing)
- *Ev pirtûk yên wan in.* These books are theirs. (**yên** for plural)

To ask whose: *Ev ya kê ye?* Whose is this?

skills.grammarMd:
Kurmancî says “I have” as “of me there is”: **… min heye**.

- *Birayekî min heye.* I have a brother.
- *Du xwişkên min hene.* I have two sisters. (**hene** for more than one)
- *Pisîka min tune.* I don’t have a cat.

**-ek** means *a, one*: *sêvek* an apple. Joined to the owner it becomes **-ekî** for a masculine word and **-eke** for a feminine one: *kurekî min* a son of mine · *xwişkeke te* a sister of yours.

**heye** also means *there is*: *Li baxçe sêv hene.* There are apples in the orchard.

lines.text: Baş e, baş e. Fermo… kilît, sindoq…
lines.en: All right, all right. Here we go… the key, the box…

lines.text: Ev çi ye? Hin tiştên kevn!
lines.en: What is this? Some old things!

lines.text: Ev… ev tiştê min e! Ji bo simbêl!
lines.en: This… this thing is mine! It is for a moustache!

lines.text: Bi rastî? Tiştekî ji bo simbêl!
lines.en: Really? A thing for a moustache!

lines.text: Û ev çi ye? Name ye?
lines.en: And what is this? Is it a letter?

lines.text: Naxêr, ew ne name ye… ew nexşe ye!
lines.en: No, it is not a letter… it is a map!

lines.text: Nexşeya Sêvanê ye! Ev gund e, ev baxçe ye…
lines.en: It is a map of Sêvan! This is the village, this is the orchard…

lines.text: Û ev çi ye, li vir? Nexşe ya kê ye?
lines.en: And what is this, here? Whose map is it?

lines.text: Ya kê ye…? Ev ne ya min e.
lines.en: Whose…? It is not mine.
